gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ taller, but genes are genes.
gaps.hint: an impossible present wish with were
gaps.explanation: For impossible present wishes, formal English uses 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more free time these days.
gaps.hint: if only plus past, present wish
gaps.explanation: 'If only' works like 'wish' and takes the past simple for present regrets: had.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ for your quick thinking, the fire would have spread.
gaps.hint: the fixed phrase if it had not been for
gaps.explanation: The fixed expression 'if it had not been for' takes the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ so pessimistic about the project.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present attitude
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present states use 'were': were not.

gaps.sentence: If the drug ___ tested properly, the side effects would have been found earlier.
gaps.hint: passive verb in an unreal past condition
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect, here in the passive: had been.
